chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu al-Khazraj, who said: Fuzayl ibn Uthman al-Awr narrated to me from al-Zuhri.

He said: I was an official for the Banu Umayya, so I killed a man. I asked Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) after that, 'What should I do with it?' He said: 'Present the blood money (diyah) to his people.' I presented it, but they refused, and I strove (to persuade them), but they refused.

So I informed Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) of that, and he said: 'Go with a group of your people and have them bear witness upon them.' I did so, but they refused (to witness). So they bore witness upon them. I returned to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and informed him.

He said: 'Take the blood money and bundle it separately, then go to the door during the time of Dhuhr or Fajr, and throw it into the house. Whoever takes anything, it will be counted for you as part of the blood money. For the time of Dhuhr and Fajr is an hour when the people of the house come out.'

Al-Zuhri said: 'I did that, and had it not been for Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), I would have been destroyed.' He said: 'And one of our companions narrated to me that al-Zuhri had struck a man with wounds, and he died from his strike.'

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or compensation for killing

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn advise resolving the issue of refused blood money?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money) in Shia tradition, specifically addressing the scenario where the victim's heirs refuse voluntary payment. Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) prescribed a method of 'secret distribution' by casting the money at the door during times of household activity, ensuring the heirs' acceptance without requiring their explicit consent. This narrative highlights the flexibility in Islamic law to resolve disputes and clear the killer's spiritual and legal debt through innovative, context-sensitive solutions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abu Al Khazraj, from Fuzayl Bin Usman Al Awr, from Al Zahry who said,

‘I was an office bearer for the Clan of Umayya, so I killed a man. So I asked Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> after that, how I should deal with it, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Present the wergild to his people’. So I presented it, but they refused, and I strived, but they (still) refused.

So I informed Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> of that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go with a number of your people, so let them bear witness upon them’. So I did it, but they refused. So they bore witness upon them. So I returned to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> and informed him<sup>asws</sup>.

Heasws said: ‘Take the wergild and make separate packages of these, then go to the door (of the guardians of the killed one) during the time of Al-Zuhr, or Al-Fajr, so throw these in the doorways. So the one who takes anything, so it would be counted for you with regards to the wergild. So when it is the time of Al-Zuhr and Al-Fajr, during these timings the people of the house come out’.

Al-Zahry said, ‘I did that, and had it not been for Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, I would have been destroyed’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And one of our companions has narrated to me that Al-Zahry had struck a man with ulcerated wounds, so he had died from his strike’.
